children.text: 检查剧本日志。
福林前往吉隆坡
福林特工失踪

你和福林在皇家雪兰莪俱乐部碰头。这是一栋尖顶的复合建筑，外面是一大片修剪整齐的草地。俱乐部的会员正在草地上举办板球比赛，而你和福林则在讨论同志会在关注什么，以及朱三娘可能的目的。“等等。”福林突然停下，瞪着外面富有的侨民。你也转过头去，看向人群。一个皮肤雪白、头发乌黑的女子背朝你们，转着一把亮红的阳伞。

“好吧，这下简单了。”福林笑道。他站了起来，兴致颇高，还给了服务员一大笔小费。但你能听出他的声音中强硬的色彩。“咱们去看看她要干什么，嗯？”

• 在剧本日志中，记录福林重归特别小组。任意一位调查员可以选择将福林探员剧情支援加入其牌库。这张卡牌不计入其牌库卡牌张数。这张卡牌可以在环球漫游• 进入冒险设置。

你到了吉隆坡，内心的恐惧在噬咬。你正在讲价去火车站要多少钱，内心不安的预感越演越烈。空气中弥漫着浓郁的醉人气味：是浸透汤汁的肉食，是槟榔咀嚼的味道，是一把一把的香料。这些气味充斥了你的感官，提醒你离家已有多远。司机将你扔在了人声鼎沸的火车站外面。你去了月台，也问了火车办公室，但都碰了一鼻子灰。

你在火车奔涌的气流中看到一把亮红色的伞，持伞的是一位乌黑头发的美丽女子。你还没来得及反应，她就已经融入人流。你禁不住想：这是一场不可思议的偶遇，还是同志会的陷阱？但无论如何，这都是你现在唯一的线索。

进入冒险设置。
收集以下遭遇组的所有卡牌：苦痛之影、黑暗笼罩、处处神秘、猩红巫术、腐败扩散、恐惧打击。
将吉隆坡火车站(东翼)、吉隆坡火车站(西翼)、雪兰莪俱乐部、雪兰莪俱乐部草坪地点放置入场。
将其他所有地点(美拉提的商店、锡矿、哇扬皮影偶戏剧场)放在一边，位于场外。
检查剧本日志。
如果福林重归特别小组，每位调查员从雪兰莪俱乐部开始游戏。如果有调查员将福林探员剧情支援加入了自己牌库，该调查员可以查找自己牌库，找出福林探员，放置入场，由自己控制，然后混洗自己牌库。在本场冒险的剩余时间内，他不占用盟友槽位。
如果福林特工失踪，每位调查员从吉隆坡火车站(西翼)开始游戏。
在每种灵怪敌人中各随机选择一张(诡怪的阴影、被掩埋的矿工、被杀害的工头)，放在一边，位于场外。将这些灵怪敌人的其他卡牌从游戏中移除。这些卡牌是双面的，其背面为剧情卡牌。为了获得最佳的游戏体验，除非受到指示，否则请勿查看其另一面的剧情卡牌。
将朱三娘敌人生成在阴影中，(红伞夫人)面朝上，并将影穑附属到她身上，动荡面朝上。结算她的隐匿关键词，将她的隐匿迷你卡牌放到起始地点以外的每个地点。
检查剧本日志中已经流逝了多少时间。
如果流逝的时间小于等于11，不作改动。
如果流逝的时间为12到18，在影穑上放置三个资源，作为充能。
如如果流逝的时间为19到26，在影穑上放置六个资源，作为充能。
如果流逝的时间大于等于27，在影穑上放置九个资源，作为充能。在当前密谋上放置1个毁灭标记。

你还没深入店铺里面，就闻到一阵醉人的芳香——低矮的天花板上垂下一捆捆干花和草药。你眼睛刚适应里面昏暗的光线，角落里就有一位身材矮小、衣着华丽的中年马来女子从凳子上起来迎接你。

“你来得有点儿晚了，但我想总比来早了好。”她一本正经地说道。你问她是什么意思，她摇了摇头：“我叫美拉提，我们的见面早有预言。”她解释说自己是个降头师，你也可以称她是萨满。魂灵已经告诉过她你会来。你问起红伞夫人的事情。

“是了，这就是我为什么高兴你没有早来。”她笑着点燃一捆芳香的药草。你感到一阵刺痛，头晕眼花，随即心神一片澄明。美拉提继续道：“那是朱三娘。她来了，我就得净化这爿店。她招来了污秽之源。兴许这就是她礼貌的缘由——她得遮住自己不洁的灵魂。”美拉提说着陷入一股模糊的疑云，仿佛自己有什么东西无处安放。你问她朱夫人想要什么。

“我真的记不得她向我要什么了。”
仅当有调查员具备法师或感知特性才能阅读：你研究了一番美拉提的气场，意识到她正受一股强大力量的操控，可能是有法术清除了她们对话中特定内容的记忆。这效果看来并不持久，但你好奇红伞夫人到底想掩盖什么。

降头师默念咒文，完成了净化仪式。她一手按住太阳穴，眉头紧皱，痛苦地跪了下来。你帮她站起，她伸出一只手扶着矮木桌，滑着坐下，示意你坐到她旁边。

“现在我懂他们为什么说你来了，”她勇敢地笑道，脸上深深的皱纹在昏暗的店面中显出阴影。降头师给你倒了杯茶，热气腾腾。“魂灵不得安宁。有什么东西搅动了苦痛的深潮，连这座城市也随之变化。人们来来往往，我在其中看到了黑暗的气息：不幸的乌云。而红伞夫人就在正中央。她是一切的预示者，散播痛苦和灾厄，从中收割大业的成果。”

降头师握着茶杯的手在抖，但她的声音却坚定清晰。她泡的茶朴实料足，你喝了一口，思索着当前的情况。朱三娘有一盘更大的棋，但具体是什么呢？你问美拉提魂灵是否告诉了她什么。她摇了摇头。

“我只能感知到巨大的痛苦。而这种巨大的痛苦以某种方式和红伞夫人连接在了一起。很有可能，她是以此为食，将其吞噬。”

福林重归特别小组
福林特工失踪

美拉提又俯下身子，一手抓住胸口。福林探员掏出了医疗小包，你上前帮他实施急救。降头师又摇摇头。

“不用担心我。我比任何魂灵都要强大，我能感受到他们陷入了巨大的、可怕的痛苦之中。整座城市悲伤遍地。”她叹了口气，立了起来。“我说过，这次见面不是偶然。要是我们能和魂灵对话，让他们安息，兴许就能理解朱夫人的大棋，没准还能将其化解。你能帮我一把吗？”

福林先看看你，再看看降头师，笑了。“我们一定帮你把这件事彻底解决。”

美拉提俯下身子，一手抓住胸口。你上前帮忙，发现她脉搏奇快，眼睛上翻。症状很快过去，她深深地叹了口气。“你的朋友刚刚对我说话了。李，李福林。”她一提到这个名字，你觉得自己血液都吓得凝结了。降头师点起一根蜡烛，照亮了她的眼睛。

“我很抱歉要告诉你坏消息，但他的魂灵十分痛苦。他提到了朱夫人，说她有多么残暴。即便现在，她也在痛饮他的绝望，靠它滋养。就像你我进食一样。我明白了。”她顿了顿，喝了口茶，严肃地望着你。“朱夫人以亡魂的痛苦为食。整座城市悲伤遍地。我知道我们这才刚见面，但你能帮帮我吗？”

你缓缓地点了点头，决心和愤怒同样沉重地压在你心头。

如果未达成任何结局(每位调查员撤退或者被击败): 你不堪重负，逃出了吉隆坡。朱三娘用以操纵这座城市的手段，已经开始入侵你的意志，闯入你的梦境。接下来几夜，你都一身冷汗地惊醒，发现自己想象对她弯腰，为她神秘的红伞痴迷。你发现自己闲暇时还会哼起小曲，那调子正是她在吉隆坡追逐你时口中悠扬轻快的那一支。你不禁想知道自己是否还能将她真正抛诸脑后……

一股能量在空气中起伏。力量——可怕的、骇人的力量——从你的手臂喷涌而出。朱三娘哀嚎着倒地，痛苦的痉挛。

“滚。”你发出了不全属于自己的声音，“滚得远远的，再也不要回来。”

你俯视着她，可怕的能量正在消散。朱三娘脸上满是泪痕。她站了起来，双手颤抖。有那么一瞬，她恶狠狠地瞟了你一眼，随即转身走入了雾中。

你朝朱三娘挥舞影穑，却觉得自己渐渐握不住伞了。“滚吧。”你坚决地告知她，“滚得远远的，再也不要回来。”但你的话语被她嘲讽的笑声盖过了。

“多么可悲啊。”她啐了你一口，转而望着伞。“别着急。我会回来找你的。”她用一种轻快的调子哼道。她走远的时候，你才反应过来，她不是在对你说话。影穑在你手中脉动着能量。你好奇这里面究竟藏着多少痛苦和磨难，别处又有多少人依然在受苦……

• 每位调查员取得经验值，数量等于胜利区所有卡牌的胜利X数值之和。

你在一个昏暗的房间里醒来。空气中一股浓郁的香料味道，架子上点着蜡烛。有那么一刻，你甚至想过在朱三娘手上遭受的剧痛是否只是一场梦。但你随即看到她坐在屋内远端的椅子上，唇间扬起一个残忍的笑容。

“起来。”她说道。你依令站起。

“过来。”她唤道。可怕无情的力量支配了你，你穿过黑暗，站到了她面前。

“跪下。”你听从了夫人的命令。你的余光看到一侧站着的美拉提，也被支配了。她看到眼前可怕的一幕，脸都揪在了一起。

“我们有时候定会犯错。”朱三娘说着向前轻轻拍了拍你，“你犯的错可严重了。你伤害了我，夺走了我需要的东西。不过，你所做的一切也证明了你很有价值。我能感受到你的忠诚。你忠于我吗？”虽然意志在抗拒，你的嘴还是吐出了一个词：“是的。”朱三娘点点头笑了，“这是我们伟大合作的开始。”

突然，你看见美拉提挥舞着仪式刀冲了过来。她猛击红伞夫人，你感到朱三娘对你的支配减弱了。“快走！”降头师喊道。你趁这两人扭打在一起，逃出生天。

你在吉隆坡的街上一路快走，只感到一阵深沉的疼痛嗡嗡作响。即便已经回到了酒店，你还是不能确定，自己是否还能摆脱这种为红伞夫人效命的奇怪愿望。你希望你们再也不要相见。

Intro 1: You and Flint meet at the Royal Selangor Club: a sharp-angled complex situated on the edge of a meticulously groomed lawn. A cricket match unfolds for the club members on the turf below as you and Flint discuss the Coterie’s interests and Tzu San Niang’s possible aims. “Hold on a moment,” Flint stops mid-sip and stares into the throng of wealthy expatriates. You turn your head and watch the crowd. A woman with a pale complexion and jet-black hair turns away from you, twirling a bright red parasol.

“Well, that was easy,” laughs Flint. You can hear a steely edge in his voice as he stands, gingerly, and leaves a generous tip for the staff. “Let’s see what she’s up to, shall we?”

• In your Campaign Log, record Flint rejoined the cell. Any one investigator may choose to add the Inspector Flint story asset to their deck. It does not count toward their deck size. This card can be found in the Globetrotting encounter set, indicated by • Proceed to Setup.

Intro 2: You arrive in Kuala Lumpur filled with a gnawing, terrible fear. As you negotiate the fare to the railway station, your sense of foreboding only grows. The air is full of intoxicating, overwhelming scents: juicy grilled meats, chewed betel nut, wisps of incense. All of it fills your senses and reminds you how far you are from home. After your driver drops you off at the bustling railway station, you wander the platforms and rail offices, but all your inquiries are met with blank indifference.

Amidst the steam of a retreating train, you see a brilliant red parasol held by a beautiful woman with jet black hair. You barely have time to react before she melts into the bustle, but you have to wonder: is this an unlikely coincidence, or a Coterie trap? Either way, it’s the only lead you have.

The Bomoh 1: Before you even step inside the shop, you are greeted by the intense but pleasant fragrance of dried flowers and herbs that hang in bundles from the low ceiling. The scent is intoxicating. As your eyes adjust to the dimly lit interior, a small middle-aged Malay woman in an ornate dress rises from her stool in the corner to greet you.

“You’re a bit late, but I suppose it’s better than if you had arrived early,” she says matter-of-factly. You ask her what she means, and she shakes her head. “I’m Melati. Our meeting was foretold.” She explains that she is a bomoh, or shaman, and that she was forewarned of your meeting by the spirits. You ask her about the woman with the red parasol.

“Yes, that’s why I was glad you didn’t arrive early,” she grimaces, then lights a bundle of some aromatic herbs. You feel a tingling lightheadedness wash over you, followed by soothing calm. Melati goes on: “That was Tzu San Niang. She’s the reason I have to cleanse my shop. There is a foul essence that follows her. Perhaps why she masks her unclean spirit with a veneer of politeness.” As Melati speaks, a cloud of vague confusion passes over her, as if she cannot place something. You ask her what Ms. Tzu wanted.

“I truly can’t even remember what she asked of me.”

Read only if an investigator has the Sorcerer or Clairvoyant trait: As you study Melati’s aura, you sense that she is under the sway of some powerful influence, possibly a spell that wiped her memory of any specifics of their conversation. The effects do not appear to be lasting, but you wonder what the Lady with the Red Parasol wanted to conceal.

The bomoh recites a low, mumbling chant as she completes the cleansing ritual, then holds one hand to her temple. Her brow furrows as she falls to her knees, wracked with pain. You move to help her up, and she holds one hand out, steadying herself against the low wooden table, and then slides to sit. She gestures for you to sit across from her.

“Now I understand why they told me you were coming,” she smiles bravely. The deep lines in her face fold with shadows in the dim shop. The bomoh pours you a cup of hot, steaming tea. “The spirits are restless. Something has stirred up a deep well of pain as the city reforms itself to keep up with such change. People coming and going. And in all of it, I sense a dark aura: a cloud of misfortune. And at the center of it, the lady with the red parasol. She is a harbinger of sorts. Inflicting pain and misery even as she reaps the rewards of great industry.”

The bomoh’s voice is firm and clear, even as her hands shake, holding her tea cup. You sip the rich, earthy brew as you consider the situation. Tzu San Niang has some greater design at work, but what? You ask Melati if the spirits have told her anything else. She shakes her head.

“I sense only their great pain. And that their great pain is linked, in some way, to the lady with the red parasol. It is almost as though she feeds on it. Devours it.”

Check your Campaign Log.
If Flint rejoined the cell, proceed to The Bomoh 2.
If Agent Flint is missing, skip to The Bomoh 3.

The Bomoh 2: Melati doubles over again, clutching one hand to her chest. You move to help her as Inspector Flint produces a small med kit to administer emergency aid. The bomoh shakes her head.

“Do not worry for me. I am stronger than any spirit, though I feel they are in such deep, awful pain. The city is rife with sorrow.” She sighs and rights herself. “As I said before, our meeting was not by any chance. Perhaps if we can speak with the spirits, put them to rest, we can understand Ms. Tzu’s greater aims and, perhaps, thwart them. Can you help me?”

Flint looks to you, and to the bomoh, and smiles. “We’ll help you get to the bottom of this.”

Skip to The Bomoh 4.

The Bomoh 3: Melati doubles over, clutching one hand to her chest. You move to help her, pulse racing, as her eyes roll back in her head. The fit passes, and she lets out a heavy sigh. “Your friend just spoke to me. Li. Li Flint.” Your blood runs cold as she says the name. The bomoh’s eyes glisten in the dim as she lights a candle.

“I am sorry to deliver such terrible news, but his spirit is in agony. He spoke of Ms. Tzu and her cruelty. Even now, she drinks his despair, feeds on it, as you or I consume food. I think I understand now.” She pauses, takes a sip of her tea, and looks gravely at you. “Ms. Tzu consumes the agony of the departed. Feeds on it. The city is rife with sorrow. I know we have only just met, but can you help me?”

You give a slow nod, resolve and wrath equally heavy in your heart.

Resolution 1: A crack of energy ripples through the air between you. Power—terrible, intoxicating power—courses through your arm. Tzu San Niang wails as she collapses to the ground, convulsing with pain.

“Go,” you say in a voice not entirely your own. “Go somewhere far away and never return.”

You look down at her as the terrible energy dissipates. Tzu San Niang’s face is streaked with tears, and her hands shake as she stands up. She gives you a fleeting, baleful look, then turns and walks away into the fog.

Resolution 3: You awaken in a dark room. The air is thick with incense and the shelves are lit with brightly-burning candles. For a fleeting moment, you wonder if the intense pain you felt at Tzu San Niang’s hands was a dream, before you see her sitting in a chair at the far end of the room, a cruel smile spread across her lips.

“Rise,” she says. Dutifully, you stand up.

“Come,” she beckons. Compelled by an awful, inexorable force, you walk through the darkness to stand before her.

“Kneel.” You do as your lady commands. Out of the corner of your eye, you see Melati standing, also under her sway, her own face pinched in concentration as she watches this awful scene unfold.

“Sometimes we make mistakes,” Tzu San Niang says. She leans forward and pats you gently. “And you have made a grave mistake. You have hurt me. You have taken something I need. But, also, all you were doing was proving your worth to me. I can sense your devotion. Are you not devoted to me?” Your mouth forms the word, but your mind resists as you say: “Yes.” Tzu San Niang nods, smiling. “This is the beginning of a wonderful partnership, I think.”

Suddenly, you see Melati dart forward, brandishing a ceremonial knife. As she strikes the lady with the red parasol, you feel Tzu San Niang’s grip on your will weaken. “Get out of here!” shouts the bomoh. As the pair struggle, you flee for your life.

Walking the streets of Kuala Lumpur in a haze, you feel a deep, thrumming pain. Even as you return to your hotel, you wonder if you will ever shake this strange desire to serve the lady with the red parasol. You hope you never meet her again.
